# Best portable power stations for a CPAP

These picks come from spec sheets and runtime math. Two of the guides say outright that they haven't lab-tested the units. Runtimes assume an 8-hour night.

## Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (~$700)
- It has 1,024 Wh, a 10 ms UPS switchover, and a noise rating of about 20 dB at low loads. Its wall recharge is the fastest of the group at about 49 minutes ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).
- You get roughly 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and about 1.2 to 1.7 with it on. The sources differ on the humidifier-on figure.
- It weighs 24.9 lb and can't be expanded.
- I don't have a direct purchase link for it. [BuyerSheet's CPAP page](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) lists it with Amazon and official-store buttons.

## Best value: Bluetti AC180 (about $474 with a code)
- It has 1,152 Wh, which BuyerSheet rates at about 3.1 nights with the humidifier off and 1.4 with it on.
- [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). Dealectric lists code AFF5OFF, which took the price from $499 to $474.05 in its cart test on 2026-10-21. Dealectric earns a commission on purchases through that link.
- It weighs 35.3 lb per BuyerSheet. PowerStationTips says 16.5 lb, which looks wrong.

## Best for a heated humidifier or longer outages: Bluetti Elite 200 V2 (about $854 with a code)
- It has 2,074 Wh, about 5.5 nights with the humidifier off and 2.4 with it on ([PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap)).
- [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). With code AFF5OFF the price is $854.05, tested 2026-10-25. This is also a commission link.
- At 53.4 lb it's a home-backup unit, not a travel one.

## Best if you want to grow it: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (~$719)
- It has the same 1,024 Wh as the Anker, but you can add batteries up to 5 kWh. That's about 8 nights with the humidifier on ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).
- It weighs 27 lb. I don't have a direct buy link. It's listed on the [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) page above.

## Small and cheap: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (~$279–$299)
- It weighs 10.4 lb, but the 286 Wh covers only about 0.5 to 0.8 nights. That works only with the humidifier off, unless you add an expansion battery.
- See [Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/).

## What to check before buying
- **Pure sine wave output** is a must. Every unit above has it.
- **Runtime:** a heated humidifier roughly doubles power use. Running your CPAP maker's 12V DC cord through the station's car port typically adds 10–20% runtime ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/)).
- **UPS switchover:** if the CPAP is plugged into the station and the grid fails overnight, a fast switchover (about 10 ms) keeps it running.
- **Jackery:** it states that its power stations aren't recommended for medical devices, so I'd skip it for CPAP. I haven't listed the Explorer 1000 v2 for that reason.
- **Sizing:** nightly Wh × number of nights ÷ 0.85. For two humidified nights at about 520 Wh, that's roughly 1,220 Wh. By that math a 1,024 Wh unit gives you under two humidified nights, and the Elite 200 V2 gives you comfortably more.
- **Talk to your provider:** if you depend on CPAP therapy, ask your equipment supplier about backup power for your specific machine.

If you tell me your CPAP model, whether you use the humidifier, and how many nights of backup you want, I can narrow this to one pick.
